'''Isezuka Kofun''' (伊勢塚古墳) is a [[kofun]] located in Takabe, {{ill|Chūō, Yamanashi|en|Chūō, Yamanashi|qid=Q666049|lt=Chūō, Yamanashi|1=Chūō, Yamanashi}}, Yamanashi Prefecture. It is classified as a [[Round Kofun|Round kofun]].
== Location and Historical Context ==
The Isezuka Kofun is situated on the {{ill|Sone Hill Range|ja|曽根丘陵|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sone Hill Range|qq=}} along the southern edge of the {{ill|Kōfu Basin|ja|甲府盆地|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōfu Basin|qq=}} in Chūō City. This area encompasses the Uyamadaira archaeological site, which spans periods from the {{ill|Jōmon period|en|Jōmon period|qid=Q52824|lt=Jōmon period|1=Jōmon period}} to the {{ill|Nara period|en|Nara period|qid=Q189178|lt=Nara period|1=Nara period}} and {{ill|Heian period|en|Heian period|qid=Q193292|lt=Heian period|1=Heian period}}. Along with nearby tumuli such as the {{ill|Ōzuka Kofun (Chūō City)|ja|王塚古墳 (中央市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōzuka Kofun (Chūō City)|qq=}}, the Isezuka Kofun forms part of the Uyamadaira Kofun Group.

The ancient locality name "Isezuka" is said to derive from this kofun. Notably, a kofun with the same name, {{ill|Isetsuka Kofun (Ichikawamisato)|ja|伊勢塚古墳 (市川三郷町)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isetsuka Kofun (Ichikawamisato)|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|qid=Q135505746|1=Isezuka Kofun (Ichikawamisato)}}, is also located on the Sone Hill Range in {{ill|Ichikawamisato|en|Ichikawamisato|qid=Q1204453|lt=Ichikawamisato|1=Ichikawamisato}}.

The mound is circular, measuring 29 meters east-west and 27 meters north-south, with a height of 3 meters. Investigations conducted during a survey of the Takabe Uyamadaira site in 1992 uncovered traces of a surrounding ditch, suggesting the original diameter of the mound was approximately 33 meters.<ref>''Toyotomi Village Historical Records (Volume I)'', Chapter Three, Section Seven, "49. Isetsuka Kofun".</ref>

The name "Isezuka" is thought to derive from {{ill|Ise Faith|ja|伊勢信仰|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Faith|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 伊勢神宮|1=Ise Grand Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q687168}}, as the kofun has historically been associated with [[Shinto]] practices. Currently, an {{ill|Iwakura rock|en|Iwakura rock|qid=Q11587880|lt=iwakura|1=Iwakura rock}} is enshrined atop the mound. In the ''{{ill|Kai Kokushakiki|ja|甲斐国社記・寺記|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kai Kokushakiki|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}'', the mound is mentioned as "Ise Shrine" and is described as being under the administration of the nearby {{ill|Chikurin Hachiman Shrine|ja|竹輪八幡神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chikurin Hachiman Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|qid=Q135550811|1=Chikurin Hachiman Shrine}}. During the medieval and early modern periods, it was treated as shrine territory.
== Archaeological Investigations and Burial Goods ==
Over the years, the mound has undergone multiple excavations and alterations. In 1919 (Taishō 8), it was significantly modified by local youth groups for agricultural purposes, with photographic evidence documenting the process.<ref>Refer to ''Toyotomi Village Closure Commemorative Records'', p. 26.</ref>

While the surrounding area was surveyed in 1992, the mound itself remains unexcavated. Consequently, the internal burial structure and {{ill|Grave goods|en|Grave goods|qid=Q1399692|lt=grave goods|1=Grave goods}} remain unknown. Given the prominence of the Uyamadaira area during the early to mid-{{ill|Kofun period|en|Kofun period|qid=Q459939|lt=Kofun period|1=Kofun period}}, the mound is tentatively dated to this era.

The site is presently managed by the Takabe District, and visitors are permitted to explore the mound freely. Cherry trees planted on the mound enhance its scenic appeal, offering panoramic views of the Kōfu Basin.
